title: Belly pain moving to the right lower quadrant

timeline.text: Dull periumbilical pain for about 10 hours, with anorexia, nausea and one episode of emesis
Pain migrates to the right lower quadrant; worse with coughing and movement
Diffuse guarding and rigidity, consistent with perforation and peritonitis

action.text: Antibiotics with enteric gram-negative and anaerobic coverage (e.g. ertapenem, or levofloxacin with metronidazole)

ground_truth.etiology: Appendiceal luminal obstruction (e.g. appendicolith) with secondary inflammation and bacterial invasion

speaker.opening: Kenji has had a stomach ache since last night, around his belly button, and didn't want breakfast. He thinks it's something he ate. Can you help me work out what's going on?
speaker.behaviour: Practical and calm; reports vital signs as she gets them. Kenji plays the pain down and blames food.

additional_history.says: Last night, about ten hours before I called you
No burning, and he hasn't seen any blood
Penicillin: he got a rash as a kid

injects.text: Crew ordered to the storm shelter; patient and CMO shelter with them
Text-only communication with the ground while sheltered

complicators: Penicillin allergy (added for this case; not in the crew record). No surgical capability aboard. Where carried, ertapenem stock covers about 6 days of a 10-day course.

review.notes_for_physiologist: Keyframe values are placeholders; please check the untreated trajectory against the CLiFF (worst case 22.5–37.4%, untreated phase 2 lasts 168–504 h).
